# Example and validation data

synthetic_spectra.csv contains five spectra with 1,024 points and an axis from
400 to 1,800 inverse centimetres. synthetic_spectra_truth.rds contains their
known components on a normalized scale. CSV intensities equal 4000 * X + 600.

reference_outputs.rds contains fixed numerical regression inputs and expected
outputs for both architectures at lengths 1,024 and 1,738.

Its provenance matters for what the regression test proves. The expected
outputs were produced by the original implementation, not by this R package:
the original repository code was run under legacy Keras 2 with the original
weight files to produce reference_outputs.npz in the Python radar-raman
package, and this .rds is a direct conversion of that file, agreeing with it
to float64 epsilon. The test in tests/testthat/test-reference.R is therefore a
port-fidelity check rather than a self-comparison.

X1024 holds six synthetic spectra of length 1,024 generated by the original
generator under numpy seed 3. X1738 holds three normalized random-walk curves
of length 1,738, the length of the live-cell spectra, covering a second input
length.

Tests use an absolute tolerance of 1e-5, matching the Python package so both
ports are held to the same bar. The reference was stored in float32, so
agreement is bounded by float32 rounding through the network; the observed
worst case is about 6.2e-6. Three of the sixteen component references are
identically zero, because the random-walk input contains no cosmic rays and
the ensemble model resolves no bands in it; the test names those explicitly
and requires the remaining components to carry signal, so a zero-against-zero
comparison cannot pass as a successful check.

All fixtures are included in this package.
